title: Why a Crisis Makes Time Feel Slower
hook: Ever wondered why a car crash feels like slow motion?

narration.text: During a crisis, time often appears to stretch out, lasting much longer.
This happens because your brain enters a state of heightened arousal.
Your senses become sharper, processing more information per second.
Your brain also encodes many more memories than usual during this time.
When you later recall the event, all those extra memories make it seem longer.
It is a survival mechanism, allowing for quicker reactions in danger.
So, it is not time itself slowing down, but your perception of it.
Have you ever experienced this odd time distortion yourself?

description: Discover the fascinating reason your perception of time shifts during stressful situations. It is not an illusion, but a complex interaction between heightened arousal and memory encoding in your brain. Understand how your mind adapts to moments of crisis.
topic: Why your perception of time changes during a crisis, explaining the role of heightened arousal and memory encoding.
